title: Morning Headlines
intro: A collapsing US-Iran ceasefire and a naval blockade on the world's most critical oil chokepoint dominate global attention, as trade records, a Bangkok tragedy, a World Cup semifinal, and cooling inflation fill out a consequential Wednesday.

items.title: US Reimoses Naval Blockade on Iran as Strait of Hormuz War Escalates
items.subtitle: CBS News / Al Jazeera / Bloomberg
items.summary: The US military restored its naval blockade of Iranian ports at 4 p.m. ET on July 14 and launched dozens of new strikes on Iranian military targets near the Strait of Hormuz — through which roughly 20% of world energy supplies pass — after a brief ceasefire collapsed. The renewed conflict is pushing oil prices higher and rattling global markets.

items.title: China's June Exports Hit Record $412 Billion, Surging 27% on AI Boom and Tariff Rush
items.subtitle: CNBC / South China Morning Post
items.summary: China's exports jumped 27% year-on-year in June to a record $412.39 billion, far exceeding forecasts, as soaring global demand for AI data-center hardware and buyers racing ahead of new US tariffs that took effect July 1 drove the second-largest monthly trade surplus on record. The figures underscore China's continued manufacturing dominance despite rising geopolitical headwinds.

items.title: Bangkok Music Bar Fire Death Toll Rises to 30 as Police Probe Negligence
items.subtitle: NPR / Al Jazeera
items.summary: The death toll from a fire at the Rong Beer Na Lat Phrao live-music venue in Bangkok's Chatuchak district climbed to 30, with dozens more hospitalized in critical condition, after an electrical fault in a ceiling AC unit ignited flammable soundproofing and blocked emergency exits. Thai police are investigating possible negligence after finding beer crates and furniture obstructing escape routes.

items.title: England vs. Argentina: Football's Fiercest Rivalry Renewed in World Cup Semifinal
items.subtitle: Al Jazeera / FIFA
items.summary: England and Argentina met today in the FIFA World Cup 2026 semifinal in Atlanta — their first World Cup clash since 2002 — with Lionel Messi and Harry Kane headlining a match watched by billions worldwide. The winner advances to the July 19 final at MetLife Stadium in New York/New Jersey.

items.title: US Stocks Rise to Records as June CPI Shows Consumer Prices Dipped
items.subtitle: Charles Schwab / CNBC
items.summary: June CPI data showed monthly consumer prices fell 0.1%, with core inflation holding at 2.9% year-over-year, lifting the Dow Jones above 53,000 to a record close and bolstering hopes for a Fed rate cut before year-end. Major bank earnings from Morgan Stanley, Johnson & Johnson, and BlackRock are also due today, keeping markets on watch.
